info.title: Marathon API
info.description: Channels of personal video that resume where you left off. See PLAN.md §8. Every route requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>` when the server has a token configured. Clients identify themselves with an `X-Marathon-Client` header.

get.description: Channels in guide order (by number) with what each is on. Hidden channels (PLAN.md M11) are left out unless `include_hidden=true`, and then come last.

200.description: Channels, by number, with what each is on

post.description: Moves the channel to its next item. Idempotent: if `from_item_id` is not the current item, returns the current state without advancing.

200.description: What the channel is now playing

409.description: The channel has no playable items

get.description: Tunes in: returns the current item, saved position, stream URLs, and the next item for prefetching. Records a `tuned` event.

409.description: The channel has no playable items

get.description: What the channel will play, starting with its current item, if it plays on without interruption: the same sequence playback produces, through any child channels, as long as nothing else moves the channel or its children meanwhile. Does not move the channel or record an event.

parameters.name: items
parameters.description: At most this many items (default 10, or 500 with `hours`; at most 500)

parameters.name: hours
parameters.description: Stop at the first item starting this many hours ahead or later

409.description: The channel has no playable items

post.description: Steps the channel back via its rule. Like `advance`, only moves if `from_item_id` is the current item; stays put if there is nothing to go back to.

200.description: What the channel is now playing

409.description: The channel has no playable items

post.description: Saves the playback position of the channel's current item.

409.description: `item_id` is not the current item (`stale_item`), or the channel is empty

get.description: Clients connected to their control channel, most recently active first, with what each is playing.

A client's control channel, as a WebSocket. The client must send `X-Marathon-Client`. The server sends each relayed `Action` as a JSON text message; the client sends each of its `Event`s the same way, and the server republishes them on `GET /events`. A client that connects again replaces its earlier connection.

400.description: Not a WebSocket request, or no usable client ID

post.description: Relays an action to a connected client, as if pressed on its remote. `id` may be `default`: the most recently active client. The body is parsed as JSON whatever its `Content-Type`, so a bare `curl -d` works. Delivery is best effort: the action is lost if the client disconnects before it is sent.

202.description: Handed to the client's control channel

get.description: Server-Sent Events: every event any connected client publishes, from now on. Each message's `event:` field is the event's name (`now_playing`, ...) and its `data:` a `RelayedEvent` as JSON. A subscriber that falls far behind gets a comment saying how many events it missed.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many events to return (default 50, at most 1000)

post.description: Rescans every source and rebuilds channel membership. Returns when done.

get.description: The item's media bytes. Supports `Range` requests and `HEAD`. Items from a Jellyfin source are proxied from Jellyfin, ranges included.

404.description: No such item, or its file is missing

502.description: The item's Jellyfin server failed or is unreachable

oneOf.description: Tune to the next channel up (higher number, wrapping).
Tune to the next channel down (lower number, wrapping).
Tune to the channel with this number.
Tune to the channel with this ID.
Resume playback (no-op if playing).
Pause playback (no-op if paused).
Seek by this many seconds; negative is backwards.
Skip to the channel's next item.
Step back to the channel's previous item.

Move in a direction. With nothing open, Up/Down change channel and
Left/Right seek; with the guide open, they move its selection.

Choose the highlighted thing (a channel in the guide), or show info
when nothing is open.
Close whatever is open.
Show what is playing.
Open or close the channel guide.
Cycle subtitle tracks (on/off with one track).
Switch between fullscreen and windowed.

Go quiet (e.g. the TV switched to another input): pause, save the
position, and hide the overlay, ready to wake.
Come back from standby, resuming playback if standby paused it.
Save the position and exit.

Action.description:
Something a viewer (or a program acting for one) asked for. Actions are
semantic, not device-shaped: a TV remote's D-pad, a gamepad, and arrow
keys all produce [`Action::Navigate`], and the client decides what it
means in context.

Clients log and ignore actions they do not support yet.

ActionAccepted.description:
Response to `POST /clients/{id}/actions`: the action was handed to the
client's control channel.

client_id.description:
The client the action went to (useful when the request said
`default`).

from_item_id.description:
The item the client is advancing from. If it is not the channel's
current item, the channel has already moved on and the request
returns the current [`Now`] without advancing again.

ChannelRef.description: A channel named in a resolution path (PLAN.md M11).

oneOf.description: What the channel is on, or `None` if it has no playable items.

hidden.description:
Whether the channel is hidden: left out of the guide and channel
up/down, and listed only with `?include_hidden=true`. A hidden
channel can still be tuned by ID.

item_count.description:
Number of playable (not missing) items in the channel, counting
those of its child channels (PLAN.md M11).

number.description:
The channel number. `0` for a hidden channel configured without
one.

resolution_path.description:
The channels `current` is resolved through: this channel first,
then any nested child channels. Just this channel for an ordinary
channel; empty if it has nothing to play.

ClientInfo.description:
One entry of `GET /clients`: a client connected to the control channel
(`/clients/connect`).

connected_at_ms.description:
When this connection was opened, in milliseconds since the Unix
epoch.

id.description:
The client's `X-Marathon-Client` ID; use it in
`POST /clients/{id}/actions`.

is_default.description: Whether this is the client `default` currently refers to.

last_active_ms.description:
When the client last connected or sent an event. The most recent
one is the `default` client.

oneOf.description:
What it is playing; `None` before its first `now_playing` event, or
while in standby.

standby.description: Whether the client is in standby.

ClientPlaying.description: What a connected client is playing, as far as its events tell.

resolution_path.description:
The channels the item was resolved through, `channel_id` first
(see [`Event::NowPlaying`]).

title.description: Human-readable description, e.g. `Show · S03E14 · The Injury`.

oneOf.description: An item started playing (after a tune, an advance, or a skip).

position_ms.description: Where playback started within the item.

resolution_path.description:
The channels the item was resolved through (PLAN.md M11):
`channel_id` first, then each nested child channel, ending with
the one the item belongs to. Just `[channel_id]` for an
ordinary channel; empty from clients older than nested channels.

title.description: Human-readable description, e.g. `Show · S03E14 · The Injury`.

oneOf.description: The client tuned to a different channel.

resolution_path.description:
As for `now_playing`: the channel tuned to, then any child
channels its current item comes through.

oneOf.description: An item played to its end.
Something went wrong; playback carries on where it can.

Event.description: Something that happened on a client, for observers.

EventKind.description: Kinds of playback event in the history.

status.description: Always `"ok"` when the server can answer.

HistoryEntry.description:
One entry of `GET /history`. (Not to be confused with [`Event`], what
clients publish for observers.)

channel_id.description: The channel the client was tuned to.

client_id.description: The reporting client's `X-Marathon-Client` header, if it sent one.

position_ms.description: Playback position within the item when the event happened.

resolution_path.description:
The channels the item was resolved through, `channel_id` first
(see [`Now::resolution_path`]). Empty for events recorded before
nesting existed.

resolved_channel_id.description:
The channel `item_id` belongs to: `channel_id` itself, or for a
channel with nested child channels (PLAN.md M11) the child that
supplied the item. `None` for events recorded before nesting
existed.

ts_ms.description: When the event was recorded, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

duration_ms.description: Duration, once a client or catalog provider has reported it.

missing.description: True if the file was not found by the most recent scan.

source_id.description: ID of the configured source the item comes from.

subtitles.description: Sidecar subtitles. Subtitles embedded in the video are not listed.

title.description:
Episode title if one was parsed, otherwise the file name without its
extension.

NextItem.description: An item to prefetch: what the channel will play after the current item.

Now.description:
What a channel is playing: the response to `GET /channels/{id}/now`,
`advance`, and `previous`.

oneOf.description:
The item the channel will advance to, for prefetching. Computed
without moving the channel. `None` only if it cannot be determined.

position_ms.description:
Saved playback position within `item`. This is the raw saved
position; clients apply the resume rewind and the finished threshold
(PLAN.md §1) themselves.

resolution_path.description:
The channels `item` was resolved through (PLAN.md M11): this
channel first, then each nested child channel, ending with the one
`item` belongs to. Just this channel for an ordinary channel.

warnings.description:
Problems the server stepped past to find `item`, such as a child
channel with nothing to play. Clients report each as an `error`
event; playback carries on.

resolution_path.description: The channels `item` would be resolved through, as in [`Now`].

starts_in_ms.description:
How far ahead of now the item would start, if the channel plays
without interruption from its saved position. Items whose
duration is unknown count as [`PLAN_UNKNOWN_DURATION_MS`].

from_item_id.description:
The item the client is stepping back from. Like `advance`, the
request only moves the channel if this is its current item.

duration_ms.description: The item's duration, if the player knows it.

item_id.description:
The item the client is playing. Must be the channel's current item;
otherwise the report is stale and rejected with `409`.

client_id.description: The `X-Marathon-Client` ID of the client the event came from.

ts_ms.description: When the server received it, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

added.description: Items seen for the first time.

errors.description:
Sources that could not be scanned, with the reason. Their items are
left as they were.

newly_missing.description: Items that were present before and are now missing.

restored.description: Items that were missing and are back.

updated.description: Known items whose file or parsed metadata changed.

Subtitle.description: A sidecar subtitle file attached to an item.

format.description: File format, the lowercase extension: `srt`, `vtt`, `ass`, or `ssa`.

index.description: Index used in the subtitle URL.

label.description:
Everything between the video's name and the extension (`en.forced` in
`Episode.en.forced.srt`), suitable as a track title. Empty if none.

language.description:
Language tag taken from the file name (`en` in `Episode.en.srt`), if
any.

url.description: Where to fetch the file (an absolute path on the server).
